children: Shares of Axon Enterprise fell as the company announced a new investment in drone maker Skydio and cut its outlook, citing three deployments worth around $130 million that are no longer on track to occur this year.
Shares fell 10% to $345.50 in after-hours trading on Thursday. The stock closed down 9.8% at $382.56 and had fallen 33% this year.

The public safety technology company on Thursday said it expects annual revenue to be up around 30% to between $3.61 billion and $3.63 billion, compared with a previous outlook for 32% to 34% growth. Analysts polled by FactSet currently expect revenue this year of $3.71 billion.

Axon said the updated guidance removes three Federal Dedrone deployments that were previously on pace for 2026, totaling around $130 million in revenue. If those deployments had remained on track, the company would have raised its guidance by some 200 basis points at the midpoint, it said.
One $30 million deployment was expected to take place in the third quarter, with the other two totaling $100 million previously expected in the fourth quarter.
The company posted a third-quarter profit of $57 million, or 68 cents a share, compared with a loss of $2.2 million, or 3 cents a share, a year earlier.
Stripping out certain one-time items, adjusted earnings were $1.72 a share. Analysts were expecting $1.89 a share.
Revenue grew to $908.6 million, up from $710.6 million a year prior. Analysts were expecting $934.3 million.
For the current fourth quarter, the company is projecting revenue between $990 million and $1.01 billion. Analysts are anticipating $1.07 billion.
Axon also said on Thursday that it will invest an additional $1.2 billion in Skydio, bringing the company's stake to roughly 37% at a pre-money valuation of $5.2 billion.
As part of the partnership, Axon will be Skydio's exclusive distributor for public safety in the U.S. and Canada, the company said.

"Axon is taking a major stake in one of the most valuable categories in tech, and Skydio stays free to move fast," Chief Executive Rick Smith said. "With exclusive channel rights, Axon will widen its lead in public safety drones as Skydio builds the future of American aerial robotics."
